title: Serre comparison for the graded section module
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $\mathcal G$ be a coherent [pqf-def-coherent] $\mathcal O_P$-module, write $\mathcal G(n)=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal O_P(n)$ for the twists by $\mathcal O_P(n)$ of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], put $M_{\ge 0}=\bigoplus_{n\ge 0}\Gamma(P,\mathcal G(n))$ with its graded $S$-module structure, and let $\widetilde{M_{\ge 0}}$ be the associated sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. The canonical morphism $\widetilde{M_{\ge 0}}\to\mathcal G$, whose restriction on each standard open $D_+(f)$ is induced by degree-zero localization of sections, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Stacks Project, Proposition 0BXD (coherent-proposition-coherent-modules-on-proj), last paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Mathlib Proj.toSpecZero is proper and of finite type over Spec S_0. MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmoduleZeroEquiv identifies S_0 with the field k. Hence P is compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian. Apply [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] to obtain quasi-coherence of G. Apply [lem-sc-p1-homogeneous-section-tensor-powers] to L=O(d) and f for invertibility, the locus D_+(f) and compatible tensor-power identifications.

Apply [lem-sc-p1-section-clearing-denominators-qcqs] to a section s of G on D_+(f). Obtain r and a global t in G tensor L^tensor r restricting to s tensor f^tensor r. Transport t through G whisker a_r. Naturality of section maps and the first compatibility identity give precisely the first clause.

For a restriction-zero t in G tensor O(rd), transport invertibility through a_r from L^tensor r. Source Modules/ProjectionFormula.isQuasicoherent_tensorObj gives quasi-coherence of G tensor O(rd). Apply [lem-sc-p1-section-restriction-s-torsion] to kill t tensor f^tensor n. Apply the associator and G whisker b_rd,n to this zero equality. Associator naturality and the second compatibility identity identify the resulting map with G whisker twistMul(f^n), proving the second clause.

lean.statement: theorem serreSectionModuleComparison (G : (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).Modules) (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).toRingedSpace G) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} (hf : f ∈ MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k d) : (∀ s : Γ(G, Proj.basicOpen (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) f), ∃ (r : ℕ) (t : Γ(G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (0 + ((r • d : ℕ) : ℤ)), ⊤)), (G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (0 + ((r • d : ℕ) : ℤ))).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top : Proj.basicOpen (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) f ⟶ ⊤).op t = Scheme.Modules.Hom.app ((ρ_ G).inv ≫ G ◁ Proj.unitToTwist (SetLike.pow_mem_graded r hf)) (Proj.basicOpen (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) f) s) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (t : Γ(G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (0 + ((r • d : ℕ) : ℤ)), ⊤)), (G ⊗ Proj.twist (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (0 + ((r • d : ℕ) : ℤ))).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top : Proj.basicOpen (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) f ⟶ ⊤).op t = 0 → ∃ e : ℕ, Scheme.Modules.Hom.app (G ◁ Proj.twistMul (0 + ((r • d : ℕ) : ℤ)) (SetLike.pow_mem_graded e hf)) ⊤ t = 0)
